The place

Where the Ionian breeze begins

Cape Avra sits on the cape of Mytikas, five kilometres from Preveza, where the land ends and the Ionian opens up. A wide garden of palms, agaves and shade trees runs to the garden wall. Beyond it lie the beach and the open sea.

In the evening the sun sets into the water and the mountains of Lefkada turn blue on the horizon.

Avra (αύρα) is the Greek word for the soft breeze that comes in off the sea on summer afternoons. It gave the house its name.

Why Cape Avra

Sea, garden, silence.

  • Front row on the Ionian

    The house looks straight out to open water. Swim at the beach below, then watch the light change from the garden.

  • A garden for long days

    A wide lawn with palms and agaves, shade under the pergola and room for everyone. Dinner outdoors, with the sea just beyond the wall.

  • Yours alone

    One house, one group of guests. No shared spaces, no strangers at the next table. Just your own garden and your own gate to the sea.

Location

On the cape of Mytikas

A quiet stretch of Ionian coast just north of Preveza. The long sandy beach of Monolithi runs north from here, and the ruins of ancient Nikopolis are a few minutes inland. Lefkada and Parga are easy day trips.
